stem: A startup wants lower backup storage spend while keeping fast operational recovery and quarterly long-term retention evidence. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Keep automated backups for day-to-day operational restore needs.
Keep quarterly manual snapshots and remove superseded long-term copies by policy.
Use read replicas as the only backup and retention control.
Use PITR windows alone as quarterly long-term archive evidence.
Set maximum retention and indefinite snapshot retention in every environment.

rationale: Automated backups support operational restore goals, and manual snapshot lifecycle policy controls long-term storage growth while preserving required evidence points. Read replicas do not replace backup retention strategy. PITR windows are bounded and do not provide open-ended quarterly archives by themselves. Maximum retention everywhere usually raises cost without workload-class justification.
